reason: With only finite probability ODEs and optimal TV coupling allowed, the solution must construct and use a marked nonassociative collision-tree expansion, exploit equal single-coordinate marginals to cancel singleton leaves, and relate each remaining leaf to pair survival along every edge of its root path. The weighted leaf count then satisfies an exact renewal equation whose solution yields the rate1-r(nu) without loss. The nontrivial part is designing the cancellation and selecting the correct tree statistic, not the final scalar ODE. This is a substantive nonlinear-probability argument beyond an ordinary qualifying-exam coupling estimate. I support H2 for the full selected chain; I do not infer H3 merely from the tree formalism or exact rate.
core_assessment:
representation: 948–1093 defines the symmetric bilinear recombination product, Wild coefficients, planar-tree probabilities and independent edge marks. Root partitions are disjoint and exhaustive, so the law at the root is the product of the selected leaf marginals. The stated induction checks are elementary from the displayed recursions and are not unsupported new external lemmas.
cancellation: 1118–1200 uses a product of optimal leaf couplings. Singleton/empty blocks agree after taking expectations because p and q have equal one-site marginals; independence over leaves lets that common factor be separated before bounding mismatches. No independence of coordinates within a leaf is assumed.
pair_survival: 1202–1223 bounds the number of non-singleton blocks by a union over unordered coordinate pairs. Complement symmetrization of nu gives pair containment probability at most r(nu)/2 along each fixed edge, and independent marks give its depth power. This accounts for both the n(n−1)/2 coefficient and the chosen tree weight.
exact_rate: 1231–1263 establishes the root-splitting renewal identity for the probability of a tree, then sums the additive leaf statistic. Normalization of both subtree probabilities produces the scalar factor r(nu), yielding zeta(t)=exp(−(1−r(nu))t). This replaces, and does not rely on, the merely near-optimal Carlen bound1225–1229.

core_obligations: Derive the full collision-tree/marked-partition representation from the nonlinear recursion.
Use equality of one-site marginals to eliminate all singleton leaf blocks before estimating mismatch; an indiscriminate sum over all leaves would not yield contraction.
Control leaves retaining two coordinates by their depth-dependent nonseparation probability, then compute the exact time-mixture tree weight to obtain rate1-r(nu).

proof_roadmap.step: Symmetrize the collision law, build the Wild recurrence, and turn each marked binary tree into a product over a random partition of coordinates.
Optimal leaf coupling plus singleton-block cancellation reduces the difference to leaves holding at least two coordinates; a pair union bound weights each leaf by(r(nu)/2)^depth.
Condition the tree law at its first split to get a renewal equation; the expected weight solves zeta-prime=-(1-r)zeta. Combine with TV duality.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: After ordinary finite ODE/coupling background, the task still has to design and exploit the marked collision-tree representation, cancel singleton contributions using equal marginals, and average the surviving pair weight exactly over random binary trees. The resulting contraction between two nonlinear evolutions is not a direct Markov semigroup contraction or a consequence of the old entropy-production inequality. This nonroutine combinatorial-probabilistic mechanism supports H2, subject to independent review.
